Sets and Functions

Overlap sets in pictures to see unions and intersections. Judge by eye whether a map is injective or surjective.

A union takes anything in at least one set. An intersection needs both. A complement is everything outside. Colliding or missing arrows decide injective versus surjective.

For example, some 🧑 classmates love 📚 books, while others love ⚽ soccer. Friends loving both stand in the overlap. Loving at least one puts you in the union.

Prove (A∪B)c=Ac∩Bc(A \cup B)^c = A^c \cap B^c(A∪B)c=Ac∩Bc element by element.

x∈(A∪B)c  ⟺  x∉A∪B  ⟺  x∉A and x∉B  ⟺  x∈Ac∩Bcx \in (A \cup B)^c \iff x \notin A \cup B \iff x \notin A \text{ and } x \notin B \iff x \in A^c \cap B^cx∈(A∪B)c⟺x∈/A∪B⟺x∈/A and x∈/B⟺x∈Ac∩Bc
Show proof

  1. Take an element xxx. By the definition of complement, x∈(A∪B)c  ⟺  x∉A∪Bx \in (A \cup B)^c \iff x \notin A \cup Bx∈(A∪B)c⟺x∈/A∪B.

  2. x∉A∪B  ⟺  ¬(x∈A∨x∈B)x \notin A \cup B \iff \lnot(x \in A \lor x \in B)x∈/A∪B⟺¬(x∈A∨x∈B). By the propositional De Morgan's law this is ¬(x∈A)∧¬(x∈B)\lnot(x \in A) \land \lnot(x \in B)¬(x∈A)∧¬(x∈B), i.e. (x∉A)∧(x∉B)(x \notin A) \land (x \notin B)(x∈/A)∧(x∈/B).

  3. (x∉A)∧(x∉B)  ⟺  x∈Ac∧x∈Bc  ⟺  x∈Ac∩Bc(x \notin A) \land (x \notin B) \iff x \in A^c \land x \in B^c \iff x \in A^c \cap B^c(x∈/A)∧(x∈/B)⟺x∈Ac∧x∈Bc⟺x∈Ac∩Bc. Since xxx was arbitrary, (A∪B)c=Ac∩Bc(A \cup B)^c = A^c \cap B^c(A∪B)c=Ac∩Bc.

Prove ∣A∪B∣=∣A∣+∣B∣−∣A∩B∣\lvert A \cup B\rvert = \lvert A\rvert + \lvert B\rvert - \lvert A \cap B\rvert∣A∪B∣=∣A∣+∣B∣−∣A∩B∣ for finite sets, and evaluate it for ∣A∣=5\lvert A\rvert=5∣A∣=5, ∣B∣=4\lvert B\rvert=4∣B∣=4, ∣A∩B∣=2\lvert A\cap B\rvert=2∣A∩B∣=2.

∣A∪B∣=5+4−2=7\lvert A \cup B\rvert = 5 + 4 - 2 = 7∣A∪B∣=5+4−2=7
Show proof

  1. A∪BA \cup BA∪B is the disjoint union of the three pairwise-disjoint pieces A∖BA \setminus BA∖B, B∖AB \setminus AB∖A, and A∩BA \cap BA∩B.

  2. ∣A∣=∣A∖B∣+∣A∩B∣\lvert A \rvert = \lvert A \setminus B \rvert + \lvert A \cap B \rvert∣A∣=∣A∖B∣+∣A∩B∣ and ∣B∣=∣B∖A∣+∣A∩B∣\lvert B \rvert = \lvert B \setminus A \rvert + \lvert A \cap B \rvert∣B∣=∣B∖A∣+∣A∩B∣ (both are disjoint unions).

  3. Adding the two equations gives ∣A∣+∣B∣=∣A∪B∣+∣A∩B∣\lvert A \rvert + \lvert B \rvert = \lvert A \cup B \rvert + \lvert A \cap B \rvert∣A∣+∣B∣=∣A∪B∣+∣A∩B∣ — the overlap was counted twice. Rearranging yields ∣A∪B∣=∣A∣+∣B∣−∣A∩B∣\lvert A \cup B \rvert = \lvert A \rvert + \lvert B \rvert - \lvert A \cap B \rvert∣A∪B∣=∣A∣+∣B∣−∣A∩B∣.

  4. Substituting ∣A∣=5\lvert A \rvert = 5∣A∣=5, ∣B∣=4\lvert B \rvert = 4∣B∣=4, ∣A∩B∣=2\lvert A \cap B \rvert = 2∣A∩B∣=2 gives ∣A∪B∣=5+4−2=7\lvert A \cup B \rvert = 5 + 4 - 2 = 7∣A∪B∣=5+4−2=7.
